Subject: Questions on operator licensing & SLA tiers for on‑prem deployment

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the Private deployment looked promising. Procurement has a couple of open items before we loop legal:

1) Licensing: can you confirm if operator licenses are per‑site or per‑cluster? We run 3 regional clusters and want to avoid double billing.
2) Platform fee amortization: would Redwood permit spreading the platform fee over 12 months for our finance team?
3) Support tiers: we need 24/7 oncall (pager + phone) for production with a 1‑hour P1 response and a targeted 6‑hour P2. Which tier maps to that and how is it priced?

Attached is an initial SOW template we put together (Medusa_DRAFT_SOW_v1.pdf). Can you flag the commercial items you’d need to modify?

Best,
Sarah Moss
Sr. Procurement Manager
Medusa Health

Subject: Re: Questions on operator licensing & SLA tiers for on‑prem deployment

Hi Sarah — thanks, and great to hear Medusa found the demo useful. Quick answers up front, then I’ll attach a proposed commercial sketch:

1) Operator licenses: billed per‑cluster (not per site) with a cluster defined by a single control plane and shared KV cache. For your 3 regional clusters that would be 3 operator licenses. We can discuss a multi‑cluster discount if you commit to a 12‑month pilot across all regions.

2) Platform fee amortization: yes — finance‑friendly amortization over 12 months is standard for enterprise deals. We show it as a subscription schedule on the invoice; capital accounting depends on your ERP.

3) Support tiers: our "Enterprise SRE" tier supports 24/7 oncall with 1h P1 and 6h P2 response SLA (with included runbook ops). Pricing is a percentage of the annual platform fee + per‑cluster oncall retainer.

I’m attaching our support tier matrix and a quick cost sketch for your 3 clusters (PrivDeploy_Tiers.xlsx). Ben and Marissa are copied in to confirm numbers and any credits for pilot staging.

If that looks OK I’ll produce a redline of your SOW with the billing schedule and the amortization clauses.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Solutions — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions on operator licensing & SLA tiers for on‑prem deployment

Vanessa / Sarah — adding the pricing detail. High level:

• Operator license: $60k per cluster / year (list). For a 3‑cluster commit we can apply a 10% multi‑cluster discount to the operator license line.
• Platform fee: $180k / year (covers control plane, telemetry, and basic observability).
• Enterprise SRE tier: 20% of platform fee + $12k per cluster oncall retainer.

Example (before any pilot credits):
• Operator licenses (3): $180k -> with 10% multi‑cluster discount = $162k
• Platform fee (annual): $180k
• SRE tier: 20% of 180k = $36k + (3 x $12k) = $72k -> total support line = $108k

Total ARR (list): $162k + $180k + $108k = $450k

We can offer a one‑time pilot credit equal to 25% of operator license cost for the first 3 months (applied as invoice credit) if you sign a 12‑month commitment across all three clusters. That reduces first‑quarter cashflow pressure for Medusa while keeping the amortization simple.

Marissa — please confirm the language we should add around amortization and invoice schedule.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — a couple operational clarifications to make sure legal can sign quickly:

1) Invoice schedule: we’ll issue a single annual invoice by default, but we’ll add a subscription schedule to split into 4 quarterly payments on your request. Amortization on Redwood’s side will be reflected as a 12‑month revenue recognition schedule; it won’t affect the 12‑month contract commitment.

2) Pilot credit mechanics: pilot credit is invoiced and then applied as a credit memo (visible on the invoice line). We can also structure it as a waiver if your legal needs avoid credits on paper — happy to work through that.

3) Change control for cluster additions: adding a new cluster mid‑term triggers a pro‑rated operator license for the remainder of the term. We’ll include a 30‑day cooling period for capacity verification before billing.

I’ll produce a redline of your SOW that adds the quarterly invoice schedule option and the pilot credit language. Expect that in the morning (I’m attaching the proposed language in the Excel).

—
Marissa Cole
Manager, Commercial Operations
